title: Model-specific runtime optimizations: Llama / Mistral / Qwen (GQA/MQA tuning)
author: Ava Chen
description: Motivation: several customer workloads and internal benchmarks show model-specific execution patterns (GQA vs MQA for Llama variants, short-sequence attention characteristics for Mistral, and Qwen KV layout quirks) that the generic kernel and scheduling heuristics do not handle optimally. This PR introduces heuristic detection for GQA/MQA formats, selective kernel selection (fused vs generic attention) based on model and sequence-length distributions, and KV cache replay avoidance for Qwen-style layouts. Summary of changes: 1) model heuristics: auto-detect GQA vs MQA from model metadata + fallback override flag; 2) kernel selector: add confidence-weighted scoring for available attention kernels and prefer fused/k-custom kernels when expected speedup > threshold; 3) KV cache: add a lightweight Qwen layout detector and avoid unnecessary cache reshuffles by introducing an in-place aliasing path; 4) continuous batching & scheduler tweaks: bias scheduler to favor batch packing for MQA when stride patterns match; 5) tests and benches: new unit tests and bench harnesses for representative Llama/Mistral/Qwen workloads; 6) opt-in feature gate with staged rollout. Impact: on our internal bench-lab across p3/p4 hardware we observe Llama-2-13B (MQA heavy) throughput +18% on common short-sequence workloads and p99 latency down ~12%; Mistral-7B sees 12-20% latency reduction for <128 token requests due to fused attention selection; Qwen-7B KV-path changes reduce KV replay overhead and improve end-to-end token throughput by ~15% on chat-like workloads. Backwards compatibility: default behavior unchanged unless the new heuristics detect a model or the operator flips the flag; all changes behind feature gate for private/dedicated customers with gradual rollout for hosted. Testing & validation: unit tests added for kernel selector and KV path, integration tests against runtime CI, and bench runs in perf-canary. We ran a 48-hour canary with traffic shadowing to confirm no regressions in correctness. Rollout plan: staged rollout to dedicated pools with canary traffic, monitor per-model regression alerts and quality evals, then wider rollout. Related work: follows up on ENG-5902 and references earlier model-tuning PRs (pr-20412, pr-31847).
commits: feat(runtime): add model heuristics for GQA/MQA detection and override flag
perf(kernel): integrate fused attention selector and scoring pipeline
fix(kv): add Qwen in-place kv aliasing path to avoid replay
chore(tests): add unit/integration tests and bench scripts for model-specific workloads
performance_summary: Llama-2-13B (MQA): +18% token throughput for short sequences, p99 latency -12%; Mistral-7B: 12-20% latency reduction for <128 tokens using fused attention; Qwen-7B: KV replay avoidance reduces memory copies ~25% and improves token throughput ~15% on chat workloads.
testing: Added unit tests for kernel selector, Qwen KV path, and scheduler heuristics. Ran full CI, integration-kernels, and benchlab on p3/p4. Deployed to perf-canary and ran 48h traffic shadowing, no correctness regressions observed.
rationale: Model architectures and tokenization/layout choices materially change which kernels and memory paths are optimal. Encoding model-specific heuristics reduces repeated fallback/replay work and lets scheduler/batching exploit common patterns without manual per-customer tuning.
